Definition: probably from κέγχρος (millet); Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth:--Cencrea.
BiblicalUsage: Kenchreai, Cenchrea, is the port of Corinth, where Paul shaved his head for a vow and where Phoebe served the church. Acts 18:18 says Paul sailed thence into Syria, having shorn his head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow. Romans 16:1 says, I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Cenchrea is the small port with a big story: a vow kept, a sister commended, and a church that sent its servants out into the world.
